name: Child of the Pure Lands (No Heritage)

system.description:
Found far and wide across the Elemental Nations and beyond, the most common heritage is no Heritage at all. Children of the Pure Lands are the true inheritors of the Sage’s ambition. With no set future, they are able to strive into any direction their own desires take them.

This Heritage describes not only the untold thousands of civilian-born and clanless shinobi, but may also be applied to those from a Clan background who did not inherit their ancestor’s blessing and must instead forge their own.

* +1 to three Primary Attribute Bonuses
* -1 to three Primary Attribute Bonuses
* Boons: Blood & Fire
* Genin Tier - When using a Skill you do not possess Skill Ranks in, add a +5 Base Chance.
* Chunin Tier - Immediately after you suffer Damage from a melee or ranged weapon, spend a Fortune Point to ignore it entirely, therefore negating both Damage and any Injuries you may have suffered. You may even use this after failing to Dodge or Parry.
* Jonin Tier - Once per Scene, you can spend a Fortune Coin to instantly cast a Jutsu you know that matches your Chakra Nature, waiving the Chakra Cost.


* Banes: Fire & Ash
* Genin Tier - Whenever you take an innocent life unprovoked, you automatically gain 1 permanent War Stain on your Nindo.
* Chunin Tier - Once per Story, when you would be incapacitated on the Peril Track, gain a Drawback.
* Jonin Tier - N/A

system.description:
Few know the true origin of this clan, if they even know them to exist at all, to hear their boasts, one would imagine their gift was a blessing from the Sage himself, a reward for their compassion, cunning, or decisiveness (the story seems to change as often as it’s told). The truth, known only to the clan’s most dedicated scholars, is surprisingly close.

Supposedly, in the previous era of unending warfare, a young man of no import worked as part of a company of gravetenders. The company, alongside a partnered group of monks (of which Order the records are conflicted), would comb over battlefields and offer rites for the deceased before burying them. It was filthy, backbreaking labor and all too often workers would find themselves falling ill with no means of paying for medicine, as had happened to the boy’s father.


The boy, desperate to earn enough to cure his ailing father, worked extra shifts, pushing his mind and body to their limit day in and out. One day, while sorting through the bodies of a particularly vicious battle, the boy discovered a beautiful necklace on the body of a deceased female warrior. Without hesitation, he pocketed it hoping to sell it to afford his father’s medicine, not knowing that the necklace was a gift from Furikagami, a capricious Kami of Winds that stir battlefields.


Seeing the boy’s theft, the god was enraged and immediately petitioned his superior, Enma, Judge of the deceased, for permission to smite the boy for his insolence. Enma, read the boy’s fate, discerning both his past and future in an instant, before making his decision.

With one hand raised Enma blessed the boy, wisps of coiling smoke from his father’s own funeral pyre infused the boy granting him an affinity with their like.

Then Enma spoke, words heard only by the boy and Furikagami, “Flee yon filial child, as far and fast as you may. For you have angered the Kami, and Furikagami has the right to his revenge. In any place where death clings to battlefields, know that his eyes be upon you and his talon shall seek your blood. Yet know your earnest heart hast also been recognized and rewarded, for you shall be untouchable by blade and arrow and all but impossible to contain.”

name: Cursed Blood: Kitsune (Scion of the Devil-Fox)

system.description:
Mysterious and Beautiful. Haunting and Seductive. Legends of many-faced tricksters dot the legends and histories of the Elemental Nations and beyond, but few are more revered and reviled than the Kitsune, God-Tricksters of the heavens and earth.
* +1 [FB], [PB], [WB]
* -1 [AB], [CB], [IB]
* Boons: Kami-Defying Mischief
* Genin Tier - You may learn Kitsune-Legacy jutsu and gain access to the special weapon, Foxfire. It is a ranged weapon calculating its distance as [3 + PB] and has the Adaptable, Empowered (Fire, Yin), and Silent Qualities. Additionally, it attacks using the Chakra Control skill, and deals damage using [FB].
* Chunin Tier - When making a Charm roll against a target with a Positive disposition towards you, you may spend a Fortune Coin to roll with Advantage. You may Dodge and Parry using Charm.
* Jonin Tier - You may spend a Fortune Coin to waive the Chakra cost of any Jutsu that alters your shape or appearance, wrapping yourself in a nigh-infallible illusion. Enemies attempting to Break the Illusion by any means roll at Disadvantage.


* Banes: Anathemic Censure
* Genin Tier - Your body mutates, taking on a bestial trait (Fox-like Ears, Sharpened Canines, A Bushy Tail, etc.). Civilians, Nobles, and Monks who see this trait for the first time immediately fall 2 steps in Disposition (to a Maximum of -40%).
* Chunin Tier - Roll an additional 1d10 Corruption die at the end of a session where you leaned into your War alignment in order to advance a personal goal. You gain a Rank on your War alignment if either of the dice are equal to or greater than your Stains.
* Jonin Tier - You gain a Special Trait, Vulnerability (Sacred), any time you are struck with a Yang or Yin-Yang jutsu made by someone with a Negative Disposition toward you, roll Terror (3d10+3 against Peril Threshold)

* +1 [PB], [CB], [WB]
* -1 [BB], [FB], [AB]
* Boons: Heart of the Swarm
* Genin Tier - Access to Aburame-Clan Jutsu & Hiden at Character Creation. Learning Aburame-clan Hiden always comes at a discount even if your chakra Nature is different from that of the technique in question. You automatically learn the [Swarm of Self] Hiden, it does not count against your Technique limit.
* Chunin Tier - When dealing damage with an Aburame Hiden you may spend a Fortune Coin to drain 1d4 chakra from the enemy.
* Jonin Tier - Your communion with your swarm is sublime, you ignore all penalties to Stealth tests and any enemy attempting to search or track you treat their non-skill rank bonuses as penalties (even if using Chakra Sensing).


* Banes: Tithe to the Hive
* Genin Tier - Your speech and mannerisms are odd and stilted. All non-Allied characters who do not have a positive disposition towards you are treated as if they have a Negative disposition. If they already have one, it is treated as if it were 1 Step more severe (to a max of -30%).
* Chunin Tier - Impressive as they are, your swarm is vulnerable to exposure, just like other insects. When suffering damage from Fire-jutsu, increase the Damage Dice to d10, if they are already d10s, then add an additional one. Additionally, when inflicted with Damage from a Smoke-jutsu roll a Toughness Test, on a failure you are Stunned until the end of your next turn (this activates only once per round.)
* Jonin Tier - Your Swarm may be vast, but this merely increases the number of targets for skilled foes. When you are successfully damaged by a ninjutsu with any of the Burst, Cone, or Explosion templates, you lose 1d4 chakra as your swarm is consumed in the assault.

boons.description: Your Doujutsu mutates into greater form. Pick Two options from the Greater Doujutsu power list. Additionally, you gain access to Uchiha secret techniques.

banes.name: The Weakest Link in the Heart
banes.description: You generate 1 less Fortune Coin at the start of each session.

banes.name: The Weakest Link in the Heart
banes.description: At the end of each session, roll an additional 1d10 Corruption die. If either of the die are less than or equal to the number of stains earned in the session, then the PC gains a War Rank on their Nindo Tracker.

banes.name: The Weakest Link in the Heart
banes.description: If a character you have a positive disposition toward is Incapacitated or Slain in combat, you become Stunned for [FB - Disposition Level] Rounds (fellow player characters are assumed to have a Friendly Disposition (+2) unless stated otherwise).

* -1 [AB], [FB], [PB]
* Boons: Tyrannical Prince of Waves
* Genin Tier - You calculate your Chakra Pool as [Tier*(BB+WB)+IB]
* Chunin Tier - Your blood and chakra are potent medical elixirs. As an action, you may choose to drop one level on either the Peril or Damage Tracker to Assist another character within 2 Strides of you. That Character rolls with Advantage on all Heal rolls to recover from Diseases, Injuries, and Wounds as well as Chakra Control rolls to break out of Genjutsu.
* Jonin Tier - Once per scene, you may spend Fortune Coins when making a Fuinjutsu roll to automatically complete the seal (1 for Basic Seals; 2 for Journeyman seals; 3 for Master seals; 4 for Grandmaster Seals, this effect cannot be used for Jinchuriki seals).


* Banes: Beacon of Passion
* Genin Tier - Enemies attempting to track you via Chakra gain +10 Base Chance.
* Chunin Tier - Roll an additional 1d10 Corruption die at the end of a session where you leaned into your War alignment in order to uncover secrets, outwit an enemy, or utterly dominate one or more enemies. You gain a Rank on your War alignment if either of the dice are equal to or greater than your Stains.
* Jonin Tier - Though mighty of body and robust of spirit, the subtler Ninja Arts escape your mastery. When attempting to resist Genjutsu, you suffer a (-5% * Jutsu Rank) penalty.
* E-Rank = 1, S-Rank =6

The origin of the Descendants of Frigid Gloom is one known by practically all whose lives border harsh mountains and frigid tundras, though most believe them to be mere folktales. Stories of herbalists, mountaineers, or even escaped slaves getting lost within the chilly peaks before a snowstorm blows in, trapping them in a blizzard.


Much detail is given to the tragedy of it all, the description of heat draining from the victim’s body, of their limbs becoming like lead, and the last vestiges of stubborn defiance being dispassionately smothered by the snow. A morbid tale often heard in such climes. A warning as much as a lesson.


Rarely, such stories have another ending. To hear it from the mouths of the survivors, just as their despair had reached its climax, when their last efforts and vitality had been worn away, and when no hope was left for them save for the soon to be comforting embrace of the Pure Lands, they beheld a woman. Though no two accounts agree completely on appearance, all such stories corroborate certain details. Skin as pale as moonlight, a figure delicate as a snowflake, and a voice so chillingly beautiful it was as if the shinigami pressed a blade upon their spine.


They knew her by no other name than Yuki-Onna, and she always arrived with a deal.


“A Life for a Life.”


Those who accept are said to be nursed back to health by the Yokai, kept in a hidden cave until the storm breaks and they are healthy enough to return home on their own, often dazed and confused, for they had been given no target to take the life of, merely let go to resume their own.


Inevitably, the day comes. Sometimes weeks or months in the future, and in the rarest case years, that the bargain must be fulfilled. They feel it again, the chill of the shingami’s breath on their spine, rousing them from sleep amidst an untimely strong blizzard. But rather than buffeting winds, instead they hear the pealing cry of a newborn. A child with skin as pale as moonlight and delicate of figure, howling into the snowy night no parent to be found.

With them is a message, scrawled cryptically in the snow. “A Life for a Life.”


And woe to those dull enough to try and slay the child rather than raise it.
